title: Shell: environment store + SET built-in + EXEC env inheritance
description: No environment exists: the env block is a fixed 2-byte empty stub (loader.c:256, ENV_BLOCK 0x5F000) and EXEC passes env_block=0 (command.c:433). Build a real master environment (PATH/COMSPEC/PROMPT vars), a SET built-in (set/list/clear), and per-process env copy passed through exec_param_block_t.env_block to the child PSP. Underpins PROMPT, PATH, and batch %VAR%.
design:
TRANCHE-E design (grounded WL-0037+ audit). Three increments, each RED->GREEN->mutation-proven->make test, SERIAL on shared files (Rule 3):
INC-1 (no shared-file risk): NEW pure-logic module os/milton/env.c + env.h -- a freestanding master environment store (fixed-capacity arena, NO libc): env_set(name,val) (upsert, upcases name per DOS), env_get, env_unset (NAME= clears), env_count/iter, and env_serialize(buf,cap)-> DOS-format block = sequence of ASCIIZ 'NAME=VALUE\0' strings + a final extra '\0' (empty env = lone '\0\0'). Host oracle test_env.c (HOSTED, like cmd_* TU). Seed PATH/COMSPEC/PROMPT.
INC-2 (command.c): NEW CMD_SET in command.h enum + cmd_classify table row; cmd_set handler: 'SET' lists 'NAME=VALUE' lines, 'SET NAME=VALUE' upserts, 'SET NAME=' clears. Wire the global master env into kmain shell loop. test via test_command + an emu DIR-style leg later.
INC-3 (loader.c): on EXEC, env_serialize the master env into ENV_BLOCK (0x5F000) and pass env_linear=ENV_BLOCK (not 0) so child PSP env_seg points at the real block (psp_build already does flat_to_fake_paragraph). Per-process: child inherits a COPY (already physically separate region). Mutation: drop the serialize -> child sees empty env -> oracle RED.
Ground truth: DOS env block format = ASCIIZ NAME=VALUE strings, double-NUL terminated (Ralf Brown INT 21h/AH=4Bh EPB + PSP:2Ch). DOS 3.0+ trailing word-count=1 + progpath is OPTIONAL nicety, deferred. Unblocks dibc(PROMPT)/atf(PATH)/xw1(batch %VAR%).
close_reason: Tranche E complete: env store (inc-1) + SET built-in (inc-2) + EXEC env inheritance (inc-3), all RED->GREEN, mutation-proven, 220 host gates + test-program emu EXEC green.

Also enables a real AH=4Dh termination-type and the InDOS flag exposure (AH=34h) for resident code.

title: INT 21h AH=33h CTRL-BREAK state + CONFIG BREAK= + BREAK built-in
description: AH=33h (get/set BREAK flag) is absent (not even recognized -> 'unknown AH'). Add the BREAK on/off state, honor it from CONFIG.SYS BREAK= and a BREAK shell built-in, and gate the ^C/INT 23h check (4tw) on it. Small, but part of authentic DOS break semantics.
notes: POST-CLOSE FIX (commit 8d3f287, from adversarial review): do_break wrote AL=normalized on AL=01h SET, violating DEC-16 3.2 ('no register other than the saved flag state changes' on SET). Fixed: SET writes no output register; oracle [er3h.2] strengthened to assert AL-unchanged; new M7 mutant (SET_WRITES_AL) proves it; calling_convention.json AH=33h stanza corrected. Bead remains closed (feature complete; this was a contract-detail correction).
close_reason: Landed (commit 7c21b0b): AH=33h Get/Set CTRL-BREAK per ratified DEC-16 -- g_break_flag (default ON), int21_set/get_break_flag seam, AH=33h dispatch (GET/SET/DL-normalize/out-of-scope-AL fail-loud), CONFIG.SYS BREAK=ON|OFF -> SYSINIT, BREAK [ON|OFF] shell built-in. Spec edits (Rule 8, atomic per DEC-16): AH=33h row in int21h_register.json + calling-convention stanza + test-spec strengthened. test-er3h + 3 mutants (no-dispatch/DL-raw/default-OFF) all RED. Host gates 99->101. Full gate 103 host + 27 emu GREEN (incl 4tw); Bochs boot leg PASS.

title: Shell built-ins: COPY and DEL/ERASE (wildcard-aware)
description: COPY (file->file, file->dir, CON->file) and DEL/ERASE are absent. AH=41h UNLINK exists in the kernel but no shell verb. Build on the wildcard engine (80k) so COPY *.TXT and DEL *.BAK iterate. COPY uses OPEN/READ/WRITE/CLOSE; DEL uses UNLINK.

title: Shell: I/O redirection (> >> <) and pipes (|)
description: The shell never scans for redirection/pipe operators (the only '>' in command.c is the prompt literal). Implement >, >>, < by re-pointing child stdin/stdout via DUP2 (AH=46h already exists) around EXEC, and | as a temp-file pipe between two children. Enables the MORE/SORT/FIND filter utilities.
notes: Dep direction corrected 2026-07-10 per AUDIT plan Phase 3 ('bsy.9 FIRST -> bsy.7 -> bsy.8 -> hsct closes'): hsct now depends on bsy.7+bsy.8; the old bsy.7->hsct dep was inverted and would have deadlocked the arc.
close_reason: Umbrella complete: > and >> (delivered by this bead's own OUTPUT increment, WL-era), < (initech-bsy.7, commit 78ad8a4), | temp-file pipe (initech-bsy.8, commit e639195), all built on JFT inheritance (initech-bsy.9, c1f7e36). Every leg has host parse oracle + mutation-proven emu gate (test-hsct-redir, test-bsy7-redir, test-bsy8-pipe + mutants). MORE/SORT/FIND filters remain tracked separately as initech-m0dc.

description: Walk the FAT + directory tree, report total/used/free, find lost cluster chains and cross-links, /F to fix. Needs subdir traversal (ti8) and the streaming cluster walk (dao).

description: The classic stdin->stdout filters. Need shell redirection/pipes (s-redir) to be useful. MORE paginates, SORT orders lines, FIND greps a literal.

title: Multi-volume drive letters A:/B:/C: + real SELDISK(0Eh)/GETDISK(19h)
description: Only ONE volume is mounted (the primary ATA slave, kmain.c:696). SELDISK(0Eh)/GETDISK(19h) are dispatched but never actually switch volume (drives >1 treated as invalid by getcwd/getdisk). Build a small mounted-volume table (A: floppy, C: HDD partition) so SELDISK switches the current drive and path 'C:\...' resolves to the right volume. Depends on partitions (k-mbr) and FAT16 (z01) for the HDD.

title: Shell built-ins: MD/MKDIR, RD/RMDIR, subdir-aware CD
description: Add the directory built-ins to COMMAND.COM (command.c classify table command.c:52-61 currently has only DIR/TYPE/CD/CLS/VER/ECHO/EXIT). CD is a fail-loud stub for any real path today (command.c:553). Wire MD/RD/CD to AH=39/3A/3B (k-dir39) and real GETCWD.

title: ANSI.SYS escape-sequence interpreter on the CON output path
description: DEVICE=ANSI.SYS sits in the CONFIG.SYS baseline (sysinit.c:43) but there is NO ESC[ interpreter -- console.c renders raw bytes, so cursor positioning/color/clear are not honored. Implement an ANSI.SYS device that parses CSI sequences (cursor move, CUP, ED/EL clear, SGR color, save/restore) on CON writes. Loads as a 509.7 DEVICE= driver.
notes: PURE FSM HALF LANDED (WL-0040, 9a5fea3): os/milton/ansi.{c,h} -- GROUND/ESC/CSI state machine emitting an action stream (PUT_CHAR/MOVE_CURSOR/ERASE/SET_ATTR/DSR/KEY_REMAP), cursor/erase/SGR + grounded ANSI->CGA colour map; host gate test-ansi (94 checks, 2 mutants). REMAINING = the CON-output-path wiring + CONFIG.SYS DEVICE=ANSI.SYS gate, tracked as initech-p96i (x3mh depends on it). x3mh stays OPEN until the wiring lands.
close_reason: COMPLETE: the pure ANSI.SYS FSM (ansi.c, Wave 1 WL-0040) + the CON-path WIRING (p96i, this wave WL-0043) both landed green. ANSI escape sequences (cursor/colour/erase) now take effect in the booted OS when CONFIG.SYS loads DEVICE=ANSI.SYS.

title: INT 21h AH=3Fh on CON (handle 0): real device line-read
description: AH=3Fh READ on a CON device handle returns 0 bytes/EOF today (int21.c:975-982) -- only the direct CON-input calls (01/06/07/08/0A) read the keyboard. Make handle-based read of CON deliver cooked line input (like AH=0Ah) so redirected/handle-driven programs read the keyboard. Pairs with 4tw (^C/break in the input path).
close_reason: Landed: AH=3Fh on CON handle 0 delivers cooked line input (line+CR+LF, count inclusive per KB Q113058) via a shared conin_cooked_line() helper extracted from do_buffered_input (0Ah byte-layout preserved -- proven by the surviving 0Ah mutants). test-x8fs + mutant. Integration caught a host HANG (conin_cooked_line spun on conin_get's no-source 0 sentinel via test_fileio's kji0 CREATNEW mutants); fixed at root cause with a host-safe EOF guard (Rule 2). I also wired the orphaned test-x8fs gate. Commit ddef39a; full gate 99 host + 27 emu GREEN.

title: Shell message-catalogue conformance oracle (ADR-0003 7.4); CD/DIR diagnostics off-spec
description: ADR-0003 7.4 requires a message-catalogue conformance oracle (diagnostic output == Appendix C verbatim). test_command.c exercises only pure tokenizer/classifier/formatter; nothing checks emitted strings vs spec/dos_messages.json -- which is why a non-catalogue CD diagnostic (command.c:531) and 'ECHO is on' (command.c:574) slipped in. Also DIR ignores its argument and always lists *.* (wrong result under valid input). This is the deferred initech-509.1 conformance work. Audit: shell no-message-catalogue-oracle + cd-noncatalogue-diagnostic + (dir-arg-ignored from summary).
acceptance_criteria: String-extraction oracle scans command.c (+ other diagnostic TUs) and asserts each user-facing literal is a MSG_DOS_* catalogue macro or a non-diagnostic UI element (mutation-proven by perturbing one diagnostic); CD diagnostic moved to the catalogue; DIR honors its path/wildcard argument; make test green.

title: ata.c: no oracle for fail-loud/error/write branches; missing BSY/DRDY-before-command; error codes collapsed
description: ata.c happy READ path is the only thing exercised (test-fs, QEMU only). No oracle drives TIMEOUT/DEVICE/NO_DRIVE-mid-poll/ARG or any write-path error branch (Rule 6: proven nothing; Rule 5: disk milestone wants tri-emulator). Protocol gaps: never waits BSY=0/DRDY=1 before writing the command register (ATA req on real hw/86Box); floating-bus check fires after the command rather than after drive-select; no IDENTIFY capacity bound; poll budget is an iteration count not a time bound. ATA error codes are collapsed to FAT12_ERR_READ by all callers, so distinct failure modes never surface. Audit: ata-blockdev ata-failloud-branches-no-oracle + ata-no-bsy-ready-before-command + ata-error-codes-collapsed.
acceptance_criteria: Boot WITHOUT --disk2 asserts FAT-MOUNT-FAIL via NO_DRIVE; a corrupt/short data image asserts the DEVICE/READ path; both mutation-proven; test-fs runs on Bochs as well as QEMU; BSY=0/DRDY=1 wait added before command writes; floating-bus check after drive-select; make test green.

title: console_init accepts degenerate geometry; no padded-pitch or 8bpp DAC oracle
description: console_init (console.c:273-290) copies lfb_pitch/width/height verbatim with no validation: pitch==0 aliases all scanlines to row 0 (silent FB corruption); width==0 draws nothing while returning CONSOLE_OK; pitch<width*bpp overruns into the next scanline. Violates console.h:84 'refuse bad input, do not scribble' + Rule 2. Test gaps: test_console.c always sets pitch==width*bpp (the 'honor pitch not width' contract is never exercised -- exactly the padded-LFB bug Bochs/86Box 24bpp hit), and the 8bpp DAC index->seafoam binding (kmain.c:548-551) has no end-to-end oracle. Audit: console console-init-no-pitch-validation + console-pitch-padding-test-gap + console-8bpp-dac-no-oracle.
acceptance_criteria: console_init returns CONSOLE_ERR_* on width==0/height==0/pitch<width*(bpp/8) and leaves console unusable; test_console adds a padded-pitch case (pitch=width*bpp+64) asserting correct scanline + untouched padding (mutation-proven by stride=width*bpp -> RED); a DAC/screendump oracle asserts idx1->seafoam, idx15->gray; make test green.
close_reason: console_init rejects degenerate geometry (width/height 0, pitch<width*bpp) via CONSOLE_ERR_GEOMETRY; added padded-pitch coverage test (pitch>width*bpp). Both mutation-proven (remove guard->RED; width*bpp stride->RED). 8bpp DAC end-to-end oracle split to follow-up (needs mode-0x13 screendump infra). make test 55h+19e GREEN.

title: Loader control-transfer asm reads jump target via memory operand after switching ESP
description: Entry asm (loader.c:323-336) does mov stack_top,%esp THEN jmp *entry_eip where entry_eip is a memory operand. Correct only because KERNEL_CFLAGS is -O0 with a frame pointer (EBP-relative locals resolve into the kernel frame). If the build moves to -O2 or -fomit-frame-pointer, entry_eip/psp_ptr/stack_top become ESP-relative and jmp *%4 dereferences the just-switched PROGRAM stack -> garbage/triple-fault. No compile-time guard pins this. Audit: loader-psp loader-asm-jmp-reads-operand-after-esp-switch.
acceptance_criteria: Load entry_eip into a dedicated register BEFORE the ESP switch (or pin the fn with an optimize/no-omit-frame-pointer attribute + a guard); behavior unchanged at -O0 and -O2; make test green.
close_reason: Entry asm loads the jump target (entry_eip) into EAX BEFORE the ESP switch and jmps via register, eliminating the only post-switch memory read. By construction optimization-safe. Demonstrated RED->GREEN at -O2 -fomit-frame-pointer (pre-fix: GREET.COM never runs; fixed: passes); no -O0 regression. The permanent -O2 coverage arrives free when the toolchain moves to -O2/i686-elf (initech-6pm/CDR-0001) -- test-exec then becomes the -O2 gate and now stays green. make test 55h+21e GREEN.

title: CONFIG.SYS larger than 1024-byte scratch is silently discarded (comment claims truncation)
description: sysinit_apply_config reads CONFIG.SYS into static char cfg_buf[1024] via fat12_read_file, which returns FAT12_ERR_BUFFER (does NOT truncate) when file>buf. So a >1024B CONFIG.SYS makes from_disk stay 0 and the user's whole file is silently ignored for SYSINIT_CONFIG_BASELINE; summary prints source=baseline masking the discard. Comment at sysinit.c:134-135 wrongly claims truncation. A 1024B CONFIG.SYS is period-realistic. Audit: sysinit-boot configsys-oversize-silent-baseline-fallback (+ sysinit-phases-no-host-test).
acceptance_criteria: Either honor truncation via incremental read, or fail loud (distinct 'SYSINIT: CONFIG.SYS too large' marker before fallback) and fix the comment; factor the file-read so sysinit_apply_config is host-drivable with an injected fake; host tests for from_disk success, oversize, FILES-absent baseline=20, FILES clamp; make test green.
close_reason: sysinit honors first 1KB of an oversize CONFIG.SYS via fat12_read_partial (trim to last line) + flags it 'source=CONFIG.SYS(truncated@1024)' instead of silently discarding to baseline (operator choice). Fixed misleading comment. New test-sysinit-oversize gate (oversize fixture, FILES=8 in first lines): RED (baseline FILES=20) -> GREEN (truncated@1024 FILES=8), mutation-proven. make test 55h+21e GREEN.

title: dos_reentry_panic serial output spins unbounded on a dead UART
description: panic.c bounds its serial spin (PSERIAL_SPIN_MAX) precisely so the fail-loud path cannot wedge. The sibling path irq.c rserial_putc (irq.c:60-66) spins while !(LSR&THRE) with NO bound; on an absent/stuck UART (common 86Box config) dos_reentry_panic hangs before it can int3 into the real panic -- defeating the loud-and-bounded guarantee. Audit: interrupts dos-reentry-panic-unbounded-serial-spin.
acceptance_criteria: irq.c rserial_putc uses the same bounded spin (PSERIAL_SPIN_MAX, drop byte on timeout) as pserial_putc; make test green.
close_reason: bcg.5: do_puts NULL-guard + INT21_PUTS_SCAN_MAX bound; RED (NULL deref segfault)->GREEN, mutation-proven. bcg.8: rserial_putc bounded by RSERIAL_SPIN_MAX mirroring panic.c (target-only port I/O; emu irq-storm serial path confirms no regression). make test 55h+19e GREEN.

title: 8259A spurious IRQ7 (0x2F) / IRQ15 (0x37) wedge the machine; no spurious-IRQ EOI discipline
description: Vectors 0x2F/0x37 are never installed with real handlers, so an 8259A spurious interrupt (INTR deasserted before ack -- electrical noise/timing) lands on isr_spurious -> permanent cli;hlt. Real-hw contract: master spurious (IRQ7) -> send NO EOI; slave spurious (IRQ15) -> EOI to master only. On period PCs (Rule 5) one line-noise glitch on IRQ7 halts the system. Audit: interrupts pic-spurious-irq7-irq15-unhandled.
acceptance_criteria: Dedicated stubs at 0x2F/0x37 checking the in-service register: master spurious IRET no-EOI; slave spurious EOI-to-master then IRET; not routed to the halt path; mutation-proven oracle; make test green.
close_reason: Dedicated isr_irq7_spurious(0x2F)/isr_irq15_spurious(0x37) stubs push real vectors; idt installs them; isr_dispatch_c applies EOI discipline (slave spurious 0x37 -> master-only EOI; master spurious 0x2F -> no EOI) then resumes. test-spurious extended to fire 0x2F/0x37, asserts vec=2F/37 (dedicated stubs ran) + resume; mutation-proven (remove installs -> RED). EOI correctness by-construction per 8259A datasheet (real spurious not deterministically triggerable). make test 55h+20e GREEN; test-boot-bochs PASS. Also fixed test_idt host stubs for the new externs.

title: Spurious/unhandled-vector ISR halts forever instead of returning cleanly
description: idt_init points all non-exception vectors at isr_spurious -> isr_common -> isr_dispatch_c, which ends in for(;;) cli;hlt (panic.c:140-142) for ANY vector. Spec says the spurious handler should print diagnostics and RETURN cleanly so a stray vector does not wedge the desktop. As written any unexpected software int / non-PIT-non-kbd hw vector permanently halts. Audit: interrupts spurious-halts-not-returns.
acceptance_criteria: Split spurious path from exception path: spurious stub emits a serial diagnostic and IRETs (isr_selftest pattern); permanent halt reserved for CPU exceptions 0-31; oracle fires an unexpected vector and asserts execution resumes; make test green.
close_reason: isr_dispatch_c now resumes (clean iret via isr_common) for spurious/unhandled vectors (vector>31, sentinel 0xFF), reserving the permanent halt for CPU exceptions 0-31. New test-spurious emu gate: BOOT_SPURIOUS fires int 0x70, asserts SPURIOUS-RESUMED + no PANIC + no triple-fault; RED->GREEN, mutation-proven. make test 55h+20e GREEN; test-boot-bochs PASS (interrupt-minefield Bochs check).

title: INT 21h AH=09h do_puts dereferences EDX with no NULL check and unbounded scan
description: do_puts (int21.c:313-331) walks bytes at EDX until 0x24 ('$') with NO NULL guard and NO scan bound. EDX==0 or a string lacking '$' walks arbitrary memory (fault on flat target / megabytes of garbage to CON). Contrast path-deref fns (NULL-check + INT21_PATH_SCAN_MAX) and do_read/write (DEC-14 guarded). AH=09h is the most common DOS output call; DEC-14's fail-loud rationale applies verbatim. Audit: int21 puts-unbounded-unguarded-edx.
acceptance_criteria: NULL check on EDX + runaway bound mirroring INT21_PATH_SCAN_MAX; no-'$' and EDX==0 fixtures; mutation-proven; make test green.
close_reason: bcg.5: do_puts NULL-guard + INT21_PUTS_SCAN_MAX bound; RED (NULL deref segfault)->GREEN, mutation-proven. bcg.8: rserial_putc bounded by RSERIAL_SPIN_MAX mirroring panic.c (target-only port I/O; emu irq-storm serial path confirms no regression). make test 55h+19e GREEN.

title: CONFIG.SYS decimal-overflow guard off-by-one (config_sys.c:76)
description: cfg_parse_uint guard 'if (v > 429496729u)' is checked before v=v*10+digit; at v==429496729 with next digit 6-9 the multiply-add overflows uint32 and WRAPS instead of saturating at 0xFFFFFFFF (the documented contract). 2^32-family values (e.g. FILES=4294967296) wrap to ~0 and clamp UP to FILES_MIN instead of DOWN to FILES_MAX. Benign (still in-range) but violates the saturation contract. Found by the wave-B CONFIG.SYS fuzzer (initech-hjv). Fix: guard 'v > (0xFFFFFFFFu - digit)/10u'. Must update the fuzzer's ref_parse_uint to the corrected saturating logic + add an explicit 2^32-family clamp-to-MAX assertion + a mutant restoring the off-by-one.
close_reason: Fixed in this commit: precise overflow guard (v > (UINT32_MAX-digit)/10), fuzzer ref updated in lockstep, off-by-one mutant added + caught. 55 host + 19 emu green.

title: harness/emu/86box.c headless driver (flatpak + Qt offscreen)
description: 86Box installed via flatpak --user. Build a best-effort headless driver (QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen, serial-to-file via generated 86box.cfg) for period-authenticity gating. Slower/looser than QEMU/Bochs; not on the fast inner loop. Front D. Relates to initech-x0i.

title: Compile-time asserts: loader exit-hook struct packing + kbd ring power-of-2
description: loader_exit_hook asm assumes a struct field offset; kbd ring assumes power-of-2 capacity. Add _Static_assert so a layout change fails the build, not silently at runtime. Front A.

close_reason: Both static asserts present: kbd ring power-of-2 added in fac5577 (kbd.h); loader exit-hook struct-offset asserts ALREADY existed (loader.c:163-170, all 4 fields). Audit over-reported the loader gap (Rule 4). No further work.

title: FAT12 mount geometry: unchecked data_sectors underflow / cluster-count bounds (fat12.c:105)
description: Mount-time geometry derivation subtracts first_data_sector from total_sectors with no underflow guard and classifies FAT type on an unvalidated cluster count. Add guards + malformed-BPB test. Front A.
close_reason: NOT A BUG (Rule 4): mount already rejects sectors_per_cluster==0 (fat12.c:80, no div-by-zero), total_sectors==0 (:92), and first_data_sector>=total_sectors/<=root_dir (:105, no underflow). Malformed-BPB edge TESTS to be added under the corruption fuzzer (initech-dnn); no code change.

title: Wire INT 24h critical-error handler to real disk-error sources (fat12.c/ata.c)
description: 509.8 implemented the INT 24h critical-error handler (presents MSG-DOS-0001, processes A/R/F, returns AL=0/1/2) and made it invokable (int $0x24 + the trap gate), but NO real kernel path RAISES it yet. Real DOS invokes INT 24h from the disk-I/O error path. Wire fat12.c / ata.c read/write failures (floating-bus, BSY/DRQ timeout, bad sector, write-protect) to invoke the INT 24h handler and honor its A/R/F return (Retry=re-issue the operation, Abort=terminate, Fail=return error to the syscall). Surfaced by 509.8 (handler exists, trigger deferred). Ref: ADR-0003 DEC-10; the Ignore=3 action is also deferred.
close_reason: INT 24h now RAISED by the disk layer + A/R/F honored: crit_blockdev wrapper (ata.c) -> int21_run_critical_error -> real int24_dispatch (MSG-DOS-0001); Retry re-issues (bounded), Abort=do_terminate(0x23), Fail propagates. Wired into kmain (mount-through-wrapper; hook armed POST-mount so no-disk boots stay graceful). Host gate test-int24-wired (19 checks, 2 mutants via lpf3); emu regression 9/9 PASS (WL-0041, db2e92d). In-emulator INT-24h-trigger gate deferred (needs a QEMU mid-file disk-fault mechanism) -- filed.

title: Build-time guard: kernel _kernel_end must stay below PROGRAM_BASE (0x20000)
description: The kernel size guards in the Makefile check only the LOADED .bin size vs KERNEL_SECTORS*512 -- they do NOT check that _kernel_end (the end of .bss, which is NOT in the .bin) stays below PROGRAM_BASE (0x20000). During 509.2 the shell kernel's .bss (cfg_fat_buf[4608]) pushed _kernel_end to 0x1FF60 -- only 160 bytes below PROGRAM_BASE -- a SILENT near-collision the existing guards could not see (the .bin still fit). A future kernel .bss growth would silently corrupt the program-load region (0x20000). Add a build-time check (extract _kernel_end via nm from each kernel ELF, assert < PROGRAM_BASE with a margin) so this fails LOUD (Rule 2) like the .bin-size guard does. Apply to all kernel variants (or the largest as a canary). Cite spec/memory_map.h PROGRAM_BASE.
acceptance_criteria: Building any kernel whose _kernel_end >= PROGRAM_BASE (or within a small margin) fails the build with a clear message naming _kernel_end and PROGRAM_BASE; deliberately bloating a kernel's .bss past 0x20000 is caught at build, not at runtime.
close_reason: Build-time _kernel_end < PROGRAM_BASE guard added to all 15 kernel .bin recipes: nm extracts _kernel_end, asserts < PROGRAM_BASE-256 (parsed from spec/memory_map.h), fails loud with actionable message. Mutation-proven (orchestrator independently: 0x1000 .bss bloat -> _kernel_end=0x20d60 -> build RED; .bin guard stayed green proving the gap closed). Current headroom: 480 bytes.

title: IO.SYS + INITDOS.SYS physical two-file kernel split (H/S/R, first two root entries)
description: Split off from 509.2: the PHYSICAL on-disk two-file partition. Build the kernel as IO.SYS (HW-dependent: resident drivers + SYSINIT) + INITDOS.SYS (HW-independent: INT 21h dispatcher/FS/arena/PSP/SFT), both Hidden+System+ReadOnly as the FIRST TWO root-dir entries; boot loads IO.SYS then INITDOS.SYS in order. This is period AUTHENTICITY (real DOS layout), carries boot-layout risk (cf. KERNEL_SECTORS in WL-0009), and is NOT capability-bearing -- deferred so the SYSINIT/CONFIG.SYS capability work (509.2) and the resident drivers (509.7) proceed first against the current single flat-binary kernel. title: test-shell keystroke-injection gate flakes under extreme CPU oversubscription
description: Surfaced while verifying initech-3pe. test-shell drives a 37-key REPL transcript via --keys-after and gates on a SHELL-DONE serial marker within a fixed 12000ms wall clock; wait_for_serial_marker for keys_after uses a hardcoded 4000ms budget. Different mechanism from initech-3pe (the screendump grab); this is the key-injection/marker-completion timing path. FIX direction: tie the keystroke gate's completion budget to a marker-driven deadline (poll SHELL-DONE up to the wall clock) rather than fixed 12s/4s, mirroring the screendump-after approach, so it degrades gracefully under load instead of false-RED.
acceptance_criteria: test-shell passes deterministically under full-core saturation (12/12 hogs) 5x; no fixed sub-budget that false-REDs a guest that is merely slow; still fails honestly if SHELL-DONE genuinely never appears.

title: FINDFIRST DTA layout deviates from real-DOS byte offsets

Real DOS 3.3 places the found-file fields at attr@0x15, time@0x16, date@0x18, size@0x1A, name@0x1E (the first 0x15 bytes are reserved/search-template). Our DIR.COM reads our offsets so it is self-consistent, but the DTA is NOT byte-compatible with real DOS -- a real-DOS program (or a differential test vs real DOS FINDFIRST) would read garbage. Decide: keep the simplified layout (document as intentional InitechDOS divergence) or correct to the real-DOS offsets. Surfaced verifying initech-509.5.

title: fat12_read_file uses 5760-byte on-stack chain[2880] scratch
description: os/milton/fat12.c:529 fat12_read_file declares uint16_t chain[2880] (~5.6KB) on the stack, sized to the 1.44MB floppy cluster count. Surfaced during initech-adf dir/read implementation; not yet a live bug on the floppy path.
acceptance_criteria: fat12_read_file no longer holds a geometry-sized array on the stack; FAT16 path cannot overflow; floppy read tests stay green.

title: Consider raising the minimum hardware target to 486+ (historical accuracy for the dBASE/Lotus/WordPerfect -> Office Space era)
description: OPERATOR NOTE (2026-06-21): On reflection + research, the hardware era for the canonical app suite (dBASE III+/IV, Lotus 1-2-3, WordPerfect) running into the Office Space-frame period skews LATER than 386 -- closer to 486/Pentium. It is well plausible and DEFENSIBLE for the FINAL InitechOS to require 486-or-later hardware. ADR-0001 currently ratifies '386+, 32-bit flat'. This is a note to REVISIT the minimum-hardware contract for PRD / north-star purposes: a 486 floor is period-honest (the FPU question -- 486DX has an on-die x87, which matters for InitechBase/SAMIR soft-float vs hardware float, Initech 123 recalc, and any FP in the apps), and it would let us assume CPUID, larger caches, and a faster baseline. NOT a decision to make now and NOT blocking current FLAIR work; record it so the next PRD/ADR pass weighs it. If adopted: amend ADR-0001 (386+ -> 486+), the PRD Sec 5 hardware contract, spec/hardware.json, and reconsider whether SAMIR's soft-float profile (ADR-0009) should gain a hardware-x87 path. Decision owner: operator + committee.
notes: Raised by operator while reviewing era hardware. Cite: ADR-0001 (386+ ratification); PRD Sec 5 (hardware contract); spec/hardware.json; ADR-0009 (SAMIR soft-float, FLOW_MAX_REGISTRY=1). Tension to weigh: period authenticity (Law 4) vs the 386+ floor already built. 486DX on-die FPU is the most consequential delta.

title: Kernel x87 FPU init (CR0.EM=0/MP=1/NE=1 + FNINIT + deterministic CW) for SAMIR numeric-on-target
description: The SAMIR engine emits pervasive x87 (fldl/fistpl/fdiv/fcomi/fldcw); the kernel has no FPU init and #NM(7)/#MF(16) route to panic, so any SAMIR numeric op would PC LOAD LETTER. Enables S8.1/S8.2 (ax9.1/ax9.2). New InitechDOS work authorized by operator 2026-06-19. ADR-by-committee will fix the exact sequence + hardware.json line.
acceptance_criteria: kernel inits x87 at boot; a freestanding x87 op runs without #NM/#MF panic under QEMU+Bochs; deterministic CW; mutation-proven (skip-init -> the op panics RED).
notes: DEFERRED by ADR-0009 DEC-01 to post-M6 end-state. M6 SAMIR uses SOFT-FLOAT (no kernel FPU). Kernel x87-ready lands only when FLAIR/Turbo-Initech want hardware FP. Not on the SAMIR-in-InitechOS push.

title: Defensive: conin_cooked_line should bound against a non-terminating BOUND conin source (not just unbound)
description: Adversarial review of x8fs flagged that the host-hang guard covers the NO-source case (g_conin_get==NULL) but not a bound-but-broken source returning 0x00 forever -> conin_cooked_line would spin. ASSESSED NOT CURRENTLY REACHABLE: the kernel binds the real keyboard (blocks for real keys, never a 0x00 stream) and the host mock (test_conin.c:129-151) FATALs on underflow ('can never hang'). So this is latent fragility, not a live defect. Defensive hardening: treat a sustained no-progress condition (e.g. repeated 0x00 with a full buffer) as EOF, or have host mocks return -1/EOF on exhaustion and handle it. Low priority -- the real (no-source) hang that cost a session is already fixed (commit ddef39a).

title: DEC-16 Fork A ON-widening: check ^C on every INT 21h call when BREAK=ON (not just CON family)
description: 4tw landed the CON-family ^C check-point (always active). DEC-16 Fork A 'C-6': when BREAK=ON, DOS widens the ^C check to every INT 21h call (disk I/O etc.), not just CON char input. Add the BREAK-gated wide check-points. From initech-4tw / DEC-16 Sec 3.3.

title: FAT16 AH=36h GET-FREE-SPACE walks all clusters through the 2-sector FAT window (O(clusters) device reads)
description: d27i's fat_freespace on FAT16 is correct (cache amortizes consecutive clusters) but touches every cluster one FAT sector at a time. If AH=36h latency matters on a period HDD, use a larger free-count window or a sequential full-FAT-sector scan. From initech-d27i followup.

title: AH=3Fh on AUX/PRN read returns EOF (no serial/parallel input driver)
description: x8fs cooked-reads only dev_id==SFT_DEV_CON; AUX(COM1)/PRN(LPT1) reads fall through to 0-byte EOF (no driver). Pre-existing limitation, documented. From initech-x8fs followup.

title: AH=3Fh on CON: buffer the over-long line remainder for the next read (KB Q113058)
description: x8fs cooked CON read handles the common case count>=line+CR+LF; real DOS leaves the unread tail of an over-long line in an internal CON buffer for the next 3Fh read. From initech-x8fs followup.

title: spec/dbf_normalization.json: locked meaningful-vs-normalize .dbf/.dbt/.ndx byte map (round-trip contract)
description: Realize PRD §6.6 'meaningful bytes' clause as LOCKED spec-data (CLAUDE.md Rule 8) so the initech-17n round-trip oracle consumes the normalization mask as DATA, not prose. Captures which .dbf/.dbt/.ndx bytes must round-trip byte-exact (version byte, counts, field descriptors name/type/len/dec, 0x0D terminator, all record bytes, memo content+pointer) vs which spans get masked to a sentinel before diffing (last-update date 0x01-0x03, language-driver 0x1D, reserved runs, per-descriptor data-address, trailing 0x1A, deleted-record payload policy, .dbt block tails, .mdx dates+garbage). Spec'd in docs/research/dbase-ground-truth.md sec 2 + 4.4. Lock + mutation-prove (flip one mask cell -> a passing round-trip must go RED).
design: Mechanical recipe: parse both files to a canonical struct; value-level diff for data; PLUS a masked raw memcmp (zero the NORMALIZE ranges both sides) to catch structural drift; bidirectional (SAMIR-writes/ref-reads AND ref-writes/SAMIR-reads). House JSON conventions: _comment provenance + status/ratification line.

description: Adversarial review of initech-nmpo: the strengthened host CREATNEW oracle leg (e) asserts 0x0003 for an empty/path-component case, but that value comes from a mock-backend limitation rather than real subdir-create behavior. The end-to-end FAT12 gate (test-nmpo) pins the real path, but leg (e)'s 0x0003 is a mock artifact. title: lpf3 fault-rollback oracle coverage gaps: mkdir set_entry-EOC-fail leg uncovered; scenario [A] on-disk asserts always-true on fault path
description: Adversarial review of initech-lpf3: the new fault-injection gate (test-fat-fault-rollback, 35 checks) leaves two gaps. (1) The fat12_mkdir set_entry-EOC-fail rollback leg (fat12.c ~2916-2926) has no DIRECT oracle (only flush-fail post-grow + create/write are driven). (2) In scenario [A] the on-disk + dir-entry assertions are always-true on the fault path -- only the in-memory free-count is the load-bearing pin; strengthen so the on-disk state is actually exercised. Also scenario [C] write-count arithmetic silently assumes num_fats==2 (add a guard if geometry changes). Strengthen the oracle to drive the EOC-fail leg + make [A]'s on-disk assertions load-bearing.

title: IOCTL AH=44h fidelity (4nbn): AL=08 takes BL=drive not a handle; AL=01 asserts an invented DX output
description: Adversarial review of initech-4nbn (both P3, benign): (1) real DOS AX=4408h (Is-Block-Device-Changeable) takes BL=drive-number on a BLOCK device, not an EBX/JFT handle; our model resolves EBX as a JFT handle and always returns AX=0x0001/CF=1 (not-applicable, since the SFT exposes no block-device handle). Documented in spec, but record as an intentional model deviation or add the BL=drive shape if a consumer needs it. (2) AL=01h Set-Device-Info is modeled as a no-op success that echoes DX=0x80D3, but real DOS 4401h does not define DX as an output -- the oracle over-asserts an invented return (WL-0025 'oracle asserts a value the contract doesn't produce', benign). Relax the AL=01 oracle to not pin DX, or document the choice.

title: test-absdisk-emu (8403) serial-capture race: flaky under concurrent QEMU relaunch (Rule 11 reproducibility)
description: Adversarial review of initech-8403: the new in-emulator gate test-absdisk-emu passed deterministically in a quiet serial 'make test' (5/5 checks: ABSDISK-BIND-OK/ABS-W26/R25/RT=OK/exit rc=0) but flaked 0/8 under rapid back-to-back QEMU relaunches racing other QEMU instances (serial_len=0, cpu_reset, EIP=0 -- guest never executes past power-on reset). test-vect (which it mirrors) is rock-solid 5/5 under the same load. Harden the serial-capture: mirror test-vect's proven-stable serial-flush/wait, and add a guard that fails with a distinct 'serial not captured (harness race) -- retry' message vs a genuine marker-missing failure. Not blocking (the gate is green the way 'make test' actually runs it).

title: test-absdisk: add a direct in-emulator int 25h/26h self-test (close the asm-stub coverage gap)
description: Adversarial review of 4mq7: the host oracle drives int25/26_dispatch DIRECTLY; the asm int25_entry/int26_entry -> dispatch -> IRETD path is NOT invoked by any host/emu gate (no in-kernel program issues int 0x25/0x26). It is provably-correct-by-identity to int24_entry (emu-proven via test-vect), so risk is low. Add a BOOT-flavored in-emulator int $0x25/$0x26 self-test (mirroring test-vect for int24) to close the gap directly. P3, not blocking.
close_reason: Landed + adversarially verified in WL-0026 (90 host + 27 emu green). Oracle-hardened (cnvp completeness reorder, 5o6o real MUTANT 8, nmpo test-nmpo-mutant). P3 follow-ups split out: fgdz/jplu/aaan/815i.

description: Adversarial review of 4mq7 (2026-06-15): the DEC-15 ADR (line 160) ratifies bad-buffer (NULL / 32-bit wrap, user_buf_ok fail) -> AL=0x0F/AH=0x0C, and the code emits it (oracle-covered by test-absdisk), but the locked spec/absdisk_int2526.json error_codes block omits that row. JSON is silent, not in conflict. Add the row + keep the test-spec[6/6] gate green in lockstep (Rule 8 locked-spec completeness).
close_reason: Landed + adversarially verified in WL-0026 (90 host + 27 emu green). Oracle-hardened (cnvp completeness reorder, 5o6o real MUTANT 8, nmpo test-nmpo-mutant). P3 follow-ups split out: fgdz/jplu/aaan/815i.

title: RENAME AH=56h: add a non-root same-dir rename success leg to test-gnrc
description: Adversarial review of gnrc (2026-06-15): the gnrc oracles exercise rename only with dir_start==0 (root). The non-root same-dir success path (\SUB\A -> \SUB\B) is unverified directly, though the underlying non-root scan/write primitives are proven by zs24/m0bp/chmod/set_time. Add a same-subdir success leg to test-gnrc (mmd ::SUB; mcopy OLD into ::SUB; mren ::SUB/OLD ::SUB/NEW.BAK), mirroring the m0bp nested pattern. P3 coverage; no code fix required (gnrc shipped clean).
close_reason: Landed + adversarially verified in WL-0026 (90 host + 27 emu green). Oracle-hardened (cnvp completeness reorder, 5o6o real MUTANT 8, nmpo test-nmpo-mutant). P3 follow-ups split out: fgdz/jplu/aaan/815i.

title: RENAME AH=56h: cross-directory MOVE (old_dir != new_dir)
description: Deferred from initech-gnrc (which implements SAME-directory rename only and returns 0x0011 NOT_SAME_DEVICE for a cross-dir EDX/EDI pair). Cross-dir move within a drive requires: dest-dir-full growth (fat12_grow_dir), an atomic remove-from-old-dir + add-to-new-dir with rollback on failure, and a .. fixup when the moved entry is itself a directory. Materially larger and higher-risk than same-dir rename. Implement once a consumer (e.g. shell MOVE, or a tool) needs it.

title: CHMOD AH=43h SET: PRM masks/ignores type bits, b53d rejects 0x0005 (intentional fail-loud deviation, operator-approved)
description: Adversarial review of b53d (2026-06-15) + RBIL 4301h: real DOS SET-attributes MASKS/IGNORES a CX with the Directory/VolLabel bit set (does NOT error), and a SET targeting a directory (dir bit cleared in CX) SUCCEEDS changing the other bits. InitechOS b53d instead rejects all these with 0x0005 -- a deliberate fail-loud hardening (Rule 2) the operator EXPLICITLY approved (2026-06-15 Q4 DOS-semantics). Recorded as an intentional Law-4 fidelity deviation; revisit only if a real DOS consumer needs mask-and-succeed. NOTE: GET-on-dir was a SEPARATE unsanctioned over-reject, fixed in the b53d F1 follow-up commit.
close_reason: Landed + adversarially verified in WL-0026 (90 host + 27 emu green). Oracle-hardened (cnvp completeness reorder, 5o6o real MUTANT 8, nmpo test-nmpo-mutant). P3 follow-ups split out: fgdz/jplu/aaan/815i.

title: INT 21h AH=44h IOCTL minors AL=01/06/07/08 (set-info, input/output status, changeable-media)
description: Deferred from initech-ro6c per operator 2026-06-15 (ratify AL=00 get-device-info first). ro6c returns CF=1/AX=0x0001 for AL!=00. Implement AL=01 (set device-info word back), AL=06 (get input status: AL=0xFF ready / 0x00 not-ready), AL=07 (get output status), AL=08 (changeable media, block-device only) as thin SFT-derived answers; ground the bits from the DOS 3.3 PRM.
notes: Adversarial review of ro6c (2026-06-15) found int21.h:63-68 mislabels the device-info bit NAMES for bits 1-4 vs the real MS-DOS char-device contract. Correct layout to ground from the PRM/RBIL: bit0=stdin, bit1=stdout, bit2=NUL, bit3=CLOCK, bit4=special, bit5=raw/binary, bit6=not-EOF-on-input, bit14=IOCTL-strings, bit15=ISDEV. The header currently has ISCIN=bit1/ISCOT=bit2/ISNUL=bit3/ISCLK=bit4 (shifted one position). These macros are DEAD today (CON=0x80D3 literal + ISDEV/STDIN are the only ones referenced) and the shipped VALUE 0x80D3 is correct, so NO behavioral impact -- but this bead MUST correct the bit-name labels (PRM-grounded) before implementing the AL=01/06/07/08 minors against them.
close_reason: Landed + adversarially verified in WL-0026 (90 host + 27 emu green). Oracle-hardened (cnvp completeness reorder, 5o6o real MUTANT 8, nmpo test-nmpo-mutant). P3 follow-ups split out: fgdz/jplu/aaan/815i.

title: Fault-injection blockdev backend (write-fail-at-Nth) to drive fat12 post-grow/own-entry rollbacks RED
description: Surfaced by the m0bp adversarial review + the m0bp agent's own follow-up flag. The blockdev_file harness has no write-fail seam, so the rollback paths in fat12_mkdir (set_entry-EOC-fail, flush-fail post-grow), fat12_create, and fat12_write_file are structurally present but cannot be driven RED by any oracle except via real disk-geometry exhaustion (which only reaches the NO_SPACE path). Add a fault-injecting blockdev backend that fails the Nth write, and oracles that drive each rollback path RED. (The immediate m0bp NO_SPACE leak is fixed separately + geometry-tested.)
close_reason: Landed + adversarially verified in WL-0026 (90 host + 27 emu green). Oracle-hardened (cnvp completeness reorder, 5o6o real MUTANT 8, nmpo test-nmpo-mutant). P3 follow-ups split out: fgdz/jplu/aaan/815i.

title: CREATNEW (AH=5Bh) robustness: assert null/no-backend/exhaustion arms + fail-loud when create() bound but open()==NULL
description: Adversarial review of initech-kji0: (1) the null-path(0x0002)/no-write-backend(0x0005)/SFT-JFT-exhaustion(0x0004) branches of do_creatnew are byte-copies of do_creat but are NOT directly asserted for AH=5Bh, so a future divergence stays green -- add direct AH=5Bh cases. (2) Latent Rule-2 gap: the existence guard at int21.c:1189 is wrapped in an "if g_file->open != 0" test, so a hypothetical backend binding create() but NOT open() would skip the existence check and let create() truncate an existing file with CF clear (opposite of CREATNEW contract). Asymmetric with do_open which treats open==NULL as a hard error. Unreachable today (g_fat_backend binds both fat_open + fat_create) -- harden defensively (panic or hard error, never silent-skip). Also confirm 0x0002 vs 0x0003 for an empty CREATNEW path against a DOS-3.3 golden.
close_reason: Landed + adversarially verified in WL-0026 (90 host + 27 emu green). Oracle-hardened (cnvp completeness reorder, 5o6o real MUTANT 8, nmpo test-nmpo-mutant). P3 follow-ups split out: fgdz/jplu/aaan/815i.

title: do_geterr: dedicated AH=59h classifier arm for 0x0050 ERROR_FILE_EXISTS
description: Surfaced during initech-kji0 (CREATNEW). do_geterr has no explicit arm for 0x0050; it falls to the UNKNOWN/IGNORE bucket. Functionally safe (the dispatch wrapper auto-notes AX=0x0050 into g_last_error and the oracle passes), but a dedicated class/action arm would be tidier. Low priority.

title: Mutation-proof the loader EXEC directory-attr guard + tighten test-zs24-exec-mutant leg A to n==1
description: Polish from zs24 L2 adversarial verification (both lenses clean; these are the only minor/nit items). (1) loader.c load_program_from_fat's directory-attr guard (~491: refuse a DIR-attr leaf as a program -> 0x0002) is correct + closes a latent 'load a directory's bytes as a .COM' hole, but no oracle/mutant exercises it (Rule 6 gap on the only new branch lacking coverage). Add an EXEC-a-directory leg (mint a fixture whose resolved leaf 8.3 name is a directory, EXEC it, assert 0x0002/marker absent) + a -DLOADER_MUTATE_EXEC_NOATTR seam proven RED. (2) test-zs24-exec-mutant leg A asserts only 'n<2' for the GREET marker; tighten to 'n==1' so a future regression that also breaks the CWD-relative bare 'greet' (count 0) is caught. Both low-risk polish; the core subdir-EXEC functionality is fully oracle-proven with 2 biting mutants.

title: FAT12 allocator: free-cluster search hints from prev+1, can falsely report NO_SPACE under fragmentation
description: Lens-2 finding during zs24 L1 verification (pre-existing, NOT introduced by zs24). fat12_grow_dir (fat12.c ~1120) and the file-extend/write paths (fat12.c ~1796, ~2056) call fat12_find_free(vol,fat,fat_len, prev+1), i.e. search for the lowest free cluster AT OR ABOVE the current tail. If all free clusters sit below the tail, allocation returns FAT12_ERR_NO_SPACE even though space exists. Mirrors the established extend convention so it is self-consistent, but a fragmented volume can spuriously fail. Fix uniformly across all three call sites (wrap-around search from cluster 2) with a fuzz case that places free clusters only below the tail. Low priority (floppy/low-fragmentation today).

title: CWD-aware DIR header: builtin_dir should compose 'Directory of A:\SUB' from GETCWD
description: Lens-3 fidelity gap (Law 4) surfaced during ut6d verification. os/milton/command.c builtin_dir (~575) hardcodes 'Directory of A:\' regardless of CWD; inside a subdir real DOS 3.3 prints 'Directory of A:\SUB'. Out of scope for ut6d (MD/RD/CD + prompt). Fix: compose the DIR header from the same cwd_display/GETCWD seam ut6d added. Add an oracle assertion (test-ut6d or test-fs) that DIR inside SUB prints the subdir header.

The 8bpp path writes only palette indices CONSOLE_BG_IDX(1)/CONSOLE_FG_IDX(15) (console.c) and kmain programs the VGA DAC (kmain.c:548-551) so those render seafoam/light-gray. test_console asserts the indices but nothing verifies the kmain DAC mapping end-to-end; the seafoam screendump gate only runs on the LFB path, not the mode-0x13 fallback. Add a QEMU mode-0x13 DAC/screendump oracle asserting idx1->seafoam RGB, idx15->light-gray after vga_set_dac, mutation-proven by perturbing one DAC channel. Needs mode-0x13 screendump harness infra. Each item gets a RED->GREEN fix + oracle or an explicit documented WONTFIX with rationale.

title: Differential oracle vs real dBASE + interoperable round-trips
description: Generate xBase programs, run both, diff (PRD §6.6). Round-trips compared on meaningful bytes (header date/reserved/lang-driver normalized). Mutation-prove goldens.

FLAIR/InitechOS host-build gotchas (proven WL-0064): (1) the dev host is 64-bit with NO -m32 multilib -- host test binaries are 64-bit, so (int32_t)(uintptr_t)ptr TRUNCATES; recover owners by MATCHING (int32_t)(uintptr_t)app == w->refCon (truncated-both-sides works on host-64 AND flat-32) + a magic tag, never cast refCon back to a pointer; use a full-width void* for per-instance state. (2) the FLAIR heap (heap.c) is BUMP + per-class LIFO free-list: flair_free does NOT roll back the bump cursor and flair_heap_avail returns size-used (bump tail only) -- so a teardown/leak oracle must assert 'avail STABLE across launch/exit cycles >=2 (free-list reuse), a leak drifts it monotonically DOWN', NOT 'avail returns to pre-launch' (which reds a correct impl). (3) Law-4 eyeball as an agent: build the image -> build/qemu_harness --disk IMG --screendump --screendump-after MARKER -> pnmtopng the .ppm -> Read the .png. (4) parallel coding lanes must verify via direct gcc to /tmp, never concurrent make (build/ race).

FLAIR mouse IRQ12 (FO-6, commit 3835b02): the dual-PIC EOI ORDER is load-bearing -- mouse_irq_handler MUST outb(0xA0,0x20) [SLAVE] THEN outb(0x20,0x20) [MASTER]; a master-only EOI leaves the slave ISR bit set and SILENTLY WEDGES all further IRQ12 (proven by the MASTER_ONLY_EOI mutant: 0 distinct FLAIR-MOUSE). A slave IRQ also needs BOTH the master cascade (IRQ2) AND the slave IRQ12 (bit4) unmasked (pic_unmask_irq12). isr.asm uses  so irq12_entry is an inert stub in the 26 non-flair kernels (mouse.o links only into flair_live) -- keeps them byte-stable. The no-wedge property is asserted by injecting >=2 mouse events and requiring >=2 DISTINCT FLAIR-MOUSE on QEMU; flair_live can't exercise IRQ12 on Bochs (640x480 ENOMODE halts before the loop) -> Bochs strict-PIC coverage is follow-up initech-<probe-bead>.

GOTCHA: 'bd create --graph <file> --dry-run' IGNORES --dry-run and ACTUALLY CREATES the issues (and so does a real run after) -- running it twice double-creates. Also the graph path SILENTLY DROPS the per-node 'deps' and 'parent' fields (they must be wired afterward with 'bd update <id> --parent' and 'bd dep add <blocked> <blocker>'). Dep rule: epics can only block epics, tasks only block tasks (cross-type sequencing uses parent-child or relate, not deps). Always verify bd stats delta == nodes created and spot-check 'bd dep list' after a graph create.

test-fat (initech-5cu) is the FAT12 differential oracle: our reader (os/milton/fat12.c via harness/diff/fat_diff/fat_dump.c) vs TWO refs -- mtools (mdir/mcopy) + independent python3 (harness/diff/fat_diff/fat12_ref.py). Assertions: (A) names+sizes triple-agree (our==python==normalized mdir), (B) per-file content our==mcopy==python, (C) the 3 fat12 unit oracles, (D) tools present else fail-loud. Fixtures: hello/second/chain/empty(0B,start_cluster 0)/block.bin(1024B=exact 2-cluster, full last cluster). FINDING: the 0x00-sentinel-stop vs skip distinction is NOT exercised by a natural minted image (trailing dir entries are all 0x00 either way) -- only the SYNTHETIC garbage-after-sentinel case in test_fat12_dir.c catches a sentinel mutation. So the differential image alone underconstrains dir-scan termination; keep the synthetic unit case.

FLAIR live compositor clips each window's chrome to w->strucRgn (desktop.c:223 paint_window_chrome(dst,w,w->strucRgn,w->strucRgn)), and the drawer's window-frame rect is region_get_bbox(w->strucRgn) (desktop.c:117). strucRgn == the window bounds rect (window.c region_set_rect). CONSEQUENCE: anything flair_draw_document_window draws OUTSIDE [left,right)x[top,bottom) -- e.g. the documentProc drop shadow at x=right/y=bottom (offset (1,1)) -- is CLIPPED OUT on the booted desktop, even though test-chrome-fidelity (host, unclipped port) grades it GREEN. Naively widening strucRgn to include the shadow band ALSO shifts bbox(strucRgn) -> the frame rect moves (frame to 560, shadow to 561) AND changes occlusion (fronts_union/visible_into) + drag-expose + FindWindow. Real Sys7 CalcDoc: struct = content+frame+SHADOW band (window-frame.md Sec 1). The fix (bead initech-9d0e) must DECOUPLE the drawer's frame rect from the clip region. Shares the strucRgn/expose math with the 5l5z event loop.

MCB arena (509.6 part 2) placement: the cleanest, LOWEST-RISK option is a per-load DYNAMIC arena over the free tail of the image region -- the loader, after copying the .COM, inits an mcb_arena over [paragraph_align(PROGRAM_IMAGE + image_size) .. ENV_BLOCK(0x5F000)), owner = the program's PSP segment (0x3000). This is the authentic DOS model (program owns memory above its image), needs NO spec/memory_map.h change (avoids the load-bearing PROGRAM_IMAGE_MAX edit), and the arena ceiling 0x5F000 stays below the env block + stack so there is no collision. Wire AH=48/49/4A behind an int21 mem-backend SEAM (like int21_set_exec_backend) so int21.c stays mcb-free and host-testable without adding mcb.c to every test link line; the kernel binds an mcb-backed backend in kmain.c (which already links mcb.c) and does the data_para->DOS-segment conversion ((arena_base>>4)+data_para).

Clock-skew gotcha (env): build/ artifacts can acquire mtimes ~tens of minutes in the FUTURE relative to the system clock, which makes GNU make skip ALL rebuilds (every target looks newer than freshly-edited sources) -> false-green/false-red oracles. Symptom: 'Clock skew detected. Your build may be incomplete.' + a mutation-proof gate (e.g. test-dosmsg-mutant [B]) fails to bite because the intermediate 'make kernel_shell.bin' is a silent no-op. FIX: 'make clean' wipes the future-dated artifacts; rebuild from clean gives clock-consistent mtimes and the gates behave. Always 'make clean' before trusting an incremental oracle run if the skew warning appears.

DESIGN STANCE (governs all naming/structure decisions): The blandness is a deliberate, rigorous design stance. Maximal genericness -> keep every canonical name and every vestigial structure, including ones that stopped meaning anything versions ago. Corporate software never deletes; it accretes and ships the cruft forever with a straight face. InitechDOS is not a parody of DOS -- it is DOS with the soul extracted and the legacy lovingly preserved. Implication: prefer generic heritage-canonical names (ADR-0003 DEC-12); implement vestigial structures (PSP, MCB arena, FCB API) IN FULL; never 'modernize away' legacy.

Host oracle hang pattern: conin_get() returns 0 (not -1/EOF) when no CON input source is bound ('host-safe default'). A cooked-line reader that loops until CR (conin_cooked_line, do_buffered_input) will SPIN FOREVER on that 0. Kernel never hits it (keyboard bound at SYSINIT) but ANY host test linking int21.c that reaches a CON read without binding a conin source hangs (found via test_fileio's kji0 CREATNEW mutants after x8fs made AH=3Fh-on-CON a blocking cooked read). Fix: guard conin_cooked_line -- no source bound + no pushback => return EOF (Rule 2: a host oracle must fail loud, never hang). Lesson: per-lane targeted gates can miss a hang that only the FULL aggregate gate exercises -- always run the full make test at integration, with a timeout.

RATIFIED OPERATOR DIRECTIVE (2026-06-21, no relitigation): FLAIR's architecture locks in TWO design choices stolen from the X Window System factoring. (1) MECHANISM/POLICY SPLIT -- the imaging/window MECHANISM (GrafPort draw verbs, blitter, region clip, event/window core) is kept SEPARATE from POLICY/DECORATION (chrome look, control look, dialog look, colors, patterns, metrics). The mechanism is policy-free and takes color/pattern/metric as PARAMETERS; decoration is a layer on top. Neither System 7 nor Win3.1 did this internally; FLAIR does -- it is invisible on screen so it is FREE under Law 4 (fidelity = look-and-feel of the artifact, not source structure) and makes every layer independently oracle-able. (2) REGION ENGINE = THE SHARED SPINE -- os/flair/atkinson/ (scanline inversion-list set algebra) is the SAME machinery behind both QuickDraw Rgn and GDI HRGN; BOTH heritages clip through the ONE engine; NEITHER heritage owns it. This is where the chimera's two bloodlines share bone. WHY: the Office Space frame has a Mac System-7 title bar AND a Photoshop/Windows menu bar on one screen; building two vertical chrome stacks duplicates the imaging engine and drifts (the preview.webp palette bug was a symptom of color-policy smeared into decoration code). Build ONE policy-free mechanism + the two heritages become two DECORATION POLICIES over it. HOW TO APPLY: re30.4 (one palette module, kill the 5 duplicated index->RGB switches) is the FIRST mechanism/policy cut -- extract color into a POLICY layer the mechanism reads from, not a dedup'd lookup baked into chrome/control/dialog. re30.5 GrafPort verbs land the imaging mechanism policy-free. To be formalized as an ADR (amends the ADR-0004/0005 FLAIR Toolbox architecture).

COMMITTEE RULING 2026-06-20 (MZ .EXE loader, ADR-0003 DEC-08a, RATIFIED no gridlock): InitechMZ = genuine MZ container interpreted FLAT. Load module is 32-bit flat code; relocations are a list of u32 flat offsets, loader ADDs flat load base (PROGRAM_IMAGE 0x30100) to the 32-bit dword at each site. Real header fields honored (e_cp/e_cblp size, e_cparhdr skip, e_minalloc/e_maxalloc -> MCB arena with real teeth + fail-loud-if-insufficient, e_cs:e_ip/e_ss:e_sp as flat offsets). A parse-only genuine-16-bit reader lives in harness/ ONLY (differential oracle, never executed). PSP unchanged; MZ path is a prologue on loader_run_plan. Overlays (AL=03h) deferred. HONESTY: may claim 'runs MZ .EXE compiled for the flat 32-bit InitechOS target'; may NOT claim 'runs genuine DOS .EXEs'.

Bochs boot SOLVED (initech-6pj): the WORKING bochsrc is romimage=/usr/share/bochs/BIOS-bochs-legacy (the 64K legacy BIOS, NOT BIOS-bochs-latest) + vgaromimage=/usr/share/bochs/VGABIOS-lgpl-latest + cpu: model=pentium + vga: extension=vbe. With this combo the tracer boots clean (S1 JMP2 S2, no faults) and INT 10h standard VGA mode 0x13 FULLY works (BDA 0x449=13, framebuffer at 0xA0000 live, readback verified). Why the others fail: BIOS-bochs-LATEST needs CMOV (P6) so it triple-faults #UD on the pentium model, and even with model=p3_katmai it triple-faults on an IDT.limit=0 interrupt in PM during POST (the WL-0014 'IDT.limit=0' fault) -- the latest BIOS is unusable on this Bochs 2.7 build. SeaBIOS bios.bin boots our OS but its vgabios does NOT drive the VGA hardware under Bochs (mode 0x13 AH=0Fh reports 13h but framebuffer writes to 0xA0000 are dropped, read 0xFF; VBE 0x4F00 returns E00). VBE 640x480 LFB is unavailable on Bochs (legacy BIOS: VBE-ENOMODE; latest: VBE-E00) -> the portable answer is a stage2 standard-VGA mode-0x13 fallback + an 8bpp console renderer. Bochs 2.7 here is a DEBUGGER build (drive headless via -rc 'c'); only rfb/term/x display plugins; harness/emu/rfb_unblock.py unblocks the rfb wait.

Bochs RFB display does NOT render VGA mode 0x13 (initech-6pj/564): even a pristine REAL-MODE fill of mode 0x13 (index 1 everywhere + DAC[1] programmed), halted before the kernel, comes back ALL BLACK over the RFB display plugin (raw framebuffer bytes 0/345600 nonzero; RFB serves the guest as 720x530 true-color 3-3-2). The OS writes the mode-0x13 framebuffer CORRECTLY -- proven 4 independent ways: (1) stage2 real-mode write/readback at 0xA0000 returns the written byte; (2) Bochs debugger write-watchpoint on 0xAF9FF fires (kernel fill reaches the high framebuffer byte); (3) host oracle test-console 8bpp 57 checks; (4) serial shows BANNER-BEGIN/text/BANNER-END through console_putc. So Bochs's RFB plugin (the only headless display in this build) cannot display chained 256-color mode 0x13 -- a Bochs RFB limitation, NOT an InitechOS bug. CONSEQUENCE: the Bochs tri-emulator gate must assert on SERIAL markers + no-triple-fault (resolution/display-independent, the rigorous Rule-5 signal), not a screendump. A visual Bochs screendump of mode 0x13 is not achievable via RFB here; mode 0x12 (640x480x16 planar) MIGHT render on RFB (untested) but needs a planar renderer. /tmp/rfb_capture.py is the (working) RFB framebuffer-capture client.
